content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge assigns UNDERDETERMINED on a single-verse pair, so the rule governing single-verse grounds for UNDERDETERMINED applies.", "verdict": "CLEAN", "quote": "UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase 'thy father' is immediately qualified by the child's reference to 'my Father's business.'", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.", "room": "'does not state a link or its contrary': read narrowly, the rule bars only silence-based verdicts; read broadly, it could bar any UNDERDETERMINED resting on one verse. The judge rests the verdict on what the verse does say (both 'thy father' and 'my Father's business'), not on what it omits, so the narrow reading decides.", "why": "The judge grounds UNDERDETERMINED in the verse's own stated content being self-qualified, not in the verse's failure to state a link or its contrary."}
